program_name: Nutritional Sciences, M.S. (includes the ACEND-accredited Coordinated Program in Dietetics concentration)
department_or_school: Department of Human Ecology, College of Agriculture, Science and Technology
spring_2027_admission: Yes for the Coordinated Program in Dietetics concentration (a spring deadline is listed); spring entry for other tracks and for international applicants Not verified
spring_2027_deadline: November 15 (standing date listed for the Coordinated Program in Dietetics, no year shown; 2026-11-15 if unchanged). International deadline Not verified.
fall_2027_deadline: April 15 (standing date listed for the Coordinated Program in Dietetics; 2027-04-15 if unchanged). International deadline Not verified.
funding_summary: Not verified - search results for the Human Ecology graduate programs did not mention assistantships, stipends or tuition waivers.
notes: 1890 land-grant HBCU; the only Delaware nutrition graduate option found besides the University of Delaware. Search summary: the MS 'prepares graduates for work in the health sector or nutrition research'; the dietetics concentration has 28 credits of didactic courses plus 10 credits of supervised practice. The same department also offers a Food Science, MS (concentrations: biotechnology, food microbiology, food chemistry; fall deadline June 15; thesis research can use USDA-ARS facilities in Wyndmoor, PA; the department directory calls it 'MS Food Science and Biotechnology'). Graduate office contact shown on the Food Science MS page: 302-857-8200, gradstudieswilm [at] desu.edu. Before applying, ask whether a thesis option exists, whether F-1 students can hold GA/RA positions with a tuition waiver, and what the IELTS minimum is.

program_name: Master of Science in Dietetics and Nutrition (pre-professional track and RDN track)
department_or_school: College of Health, Department of Preventive and Therapeutic Sciences (per the program-cost page URL path)
funding_summary: University-wide, not program-specific: the UAA Graduate School assistantship page says graduate assistants receive wages, tuition remission and healthcare benefits; a minimum overall GPA of 3.0 is required; awards are competitive and made by the academic unit; a 15-20 hour/week teaching or service assistantship covers up to 9 tuition credits (10-14 hours: up to 5 credits); at most 20 paid hours/week. F-1/J-1 students cannot receive federal or state aid but 'may apply for UAA scholarships, fellowships, assistantships and some work programs'. No assistantship tied to the Dietetics and Nutrition MS was seen.
assistantship_types: GA - teaching or service assistantships awarded by the academic unit (university-wide page); program-specific positions Not verified
assistantship_covers: Wages + tuition remission (up to 9 credits at 15-20 h/week; up to 5 credits at 10-14 h/week) + healthcare benefits (university-wide page)
international_eligible_for_assistantship: Yes at university level (F-1/J-1 'may apply for ... assistantships'); availability in this program Not verified
notes: w4-b update: program cost page (dated 5-7-25) lists non-resident tuition of $1,128 per graduate credit vs $528 resident, 37 credits in total. The UAA catalog says non-resident tuition is waived for fully online UAA courses. International students must show one year of funding to receive an I-20, and need-based aid is not available to them. Still unverified: whether this MS has any GA slots and whether it is taught on campus in a format that allows F-1 status (ask the program and International Student Services).

department_or_school: Family and Consumer Science (Nutrition and Dietetics), College of Allied Health and Nursing
funding_summary: University-wide, not program-specific: full graduate assistantships at Minnesota State Mankato 'typically pay a stipend of at least $10,000 for the academic year and carry a waiver of up to nine graduate credits per semester'. Assistants must enroll in at least 6 graduate credits per semester and, under Minnesota State system policy, live in Minnesota during the appointment. About 20% of graduate students hold assistantships. One Mankato page adds 'Eligibility is determined by completion of your FAFSA' (F-1 students cannot file a FAFSA), while the international-admissions section has its own graduate-assistantships page, so F-1 eligibility needs confirmation.
assistantship_covers: Full GA: stipend of at least $10,000 per academic year + waiver of up to 9 graduate credits per semester
international_eligible_for_assistantship: Not stated (an international-admissions GA page exists, but another page ties eligibility to the FAFSA)
notes: POOR FIT for a funded research degree: the catalog describes the MS in Dietetics as 'a non-research, non-thesis ("alternative plan paper") program' that leads to eligibility for the CDR registration exam (a master's degree is required for that exam since 1/1/2024). Recorded because no thesis-based nutrition program was found in Minnesota outside the University of Minnesota (UMN Nutrition discourages faculty contact before review). St. Cloud State University: no nutrition graduate program found; its School of Graduate Studies gives graduate assistants tuition remission (stipend and, for many, the remission are taxable).

notes: Private university.
